articles.title: Home Assistant separates grid and solar battery charging
articles.dek: Separate measurements show where stored energy comes from and where it goes.
body: Home Assistant’s Energy dashboard can use separate measurements for electricity flowing from the grid and solar into a battery, and from the battery to the home and grid. Its charts use those readings directly instead of guessing the split, preventing grid charging from appearing as solar charging.

The battery editor asks whether a system measures total charging and discharging or each direction separately. Each direction accepts an energy sensor and an optional power sensor; if only power is available, setup offers to create the sensor that accumulates energy. Missing grid or solar setup produces a warning.

Petar Petrov connects the configuration, calculations and charts. Existing batteries configured with total input and output keep working. The power-flow diagram also follows the same split as the energy cards, and can show one battery discharging while another charges.

articles.title: Linux Voice Assistant encrypts its connection to Home Assistant
articles.dek: An optional key protects microphone audio, replies and satellite controls on the local network.
body: Linux Voice Assistant adds optional encryption between a Linux voice satellite and Home Assistant. Without it, microphone audio sent after the wake word, replies and control messages travel in plain text, and anyone who can reach the satellite’s port can control it.

Enabling encryption makes Home Assistant ask for a key when adding the satellite. Clients without the correct key are refused. The key stays in a local file; a companion correction keeps it out of logs that might be collected or pasted into support requests.

Miguel Angel Nubla tested the connection with a real Home Assistant installation on a NixOS desktop, including wake words, commands and announcements. Encryption remains opt-in; existing unencrypted setups keep their behavior.

pullRequests.title: Add ESPHome API encryption

articles.title: Squeezebox speakers join mixed Music Assistant listening groups
articles.dek: A Sendspin connection brings compatible older speakers together with newer players.
body: Music Assistant lets compatible Squeezebox and squeezelite speakers play in one synchronized group with Sendspin players, including Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition, and with AirPlay and Cast speakers connected through Sendspin. Previously those Squeezebox-family speakers could synchronize only with each other.

The speakers retain their own supported audio quality, display the group’s current track and use their buttons, remote controls and volume controls to operate the group. Their left, right or mono channel choices also carry into the Sendspin connection, alongside their individual audio processing.

The original Squeezebox lacks the timed-start capability needed for this connection. A device with AirPlay uses that connection in preference to squeezelite, which in turn takes precedence over Cast. Ordinary solo playback and groups containing only squeezelite speakers keep their existing paths.

articles.title: Music Assistant finds an artist’s popular songs beyond your library
articles.dek: ListenBrainz fills missing top-track lists, with music-service lookups deferred until a song is needed.
body: Music Assistant uses ListenBrainz to fill an artist’s top-track list when none of the artist’s music services supplies a ranking. The list can include popular songs outside the library, rather than ranking only the songs already in the library. With local files alone, it shows the listener’s own tracks in popularity order.

When a suitable music service is connected, the extra songs can be opened or queued without looking up the entire list first. Music Assistant finds each recording on the listener’s permitted services when it is opened or reaches playback. Web and mobile views recognize these entries and withhold actions such as favorites until the item has been found.

A service that cannot answer is reported separately from a song it does not have, so a temporary outage does not permanently discard the queued track. Saving such a queue as a playlist performs the pending lookups in the background, preserving queue order and reporting songs it cannot find.

articles.title: Trimlight Edge Pro lights gain local Home Assistant control
articles.dek: A new integration discovers controllers and controls power, brightness and static colors.
body: Home Assistant adds a local connection for Trimlight Edge Pro lighting controllers. A controller can be discovered automatically on the network or added by its address, then controlled as a light with power, brightness and static colors.

The available color controls depend on the LED type configured on the controller. Home Assistant checks its state every thirty seconds. Earlier Trimlight Edge controllers are not supported. whiteleaves makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration.

pullRequests.title: Add Trimlight integration

articles.title: Home Assistant controls each basket of a VeSync air fryer
articles.dek: Separate readings join pause, resume and stop controls, with availability depending on the fryer.
body: Home Assistant gives compatible dual-basket VeSync air fryers separate basket readings and cooking controls. Owners can stop a cook on each basket, and supported models also offer pause and resume. A separate sensor reports whether the baskets are synchronized.

Existing dual-basket sensors are renamed to identify Basket 1 and Basket 2. Alex H. tested the controls on a Cosori Turbo Tower Pro: only the selected basket reacted, resuming kept its remaining time, and stopping the last basket turned the fryer off.

Pause and resume are limited to fryers that support them, including the CS137/CS158 and CAF-DC111S-AEU. The controls do not add a command to start cooking. Alex H. makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core, alongside cdnninja’s basket readings and synchronization sensor.

body: Home Assistant adds shutter controls for Somfy RTS and io-homecontrol shutters paired with Freebox Delta or Freebox Home. It discovers the shutters and exposes opening, closing, stopping and a target position.

The integration translates Freebox’s position scale so fully open and fully closed match Home Assistant’s controls. slater0013 tested four Somfy shutters on a live Freebox Delta and makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

articles.title: ESPHome shares sensor readings over radio and direct network links
articles.dek: Makers can connect configured devices through supported radios or a direct network connection.
body: ESPHome adds configurable links for sharing sensor readings between devices through SX126x and SX127x radios, or through a direct TCP network connection. Makers can pair the links with ESPHome’s existing packet transport instead of writing the connection themselves.

The radio links wait while another packet is being received. With reliable delivery configured, they also leave time for the other device’s acknowledgement and retry lost messages without repeatedly sending colliding bursts. Related SX127x work lets a transmission run without holding up the device’s main loop.

The TCP link joins two devices, with one accepting the other’s connection. It can restrict incoming connections by address, report whether the link is connected and reconnect after a silent peer times out.

articles.title: YouTube Music mixes start sooner with fewer lookups
articles.dek: A cold-cache lab run falls from 88.5 seconds to 12.5 seconds, with service backoff retained.
body: Music Assistant reduces the wait for YouTube Music Endless Mixes after the request limits reported on November 14 made some starts take more than a minute. Similar-track selection no longer fetches every artist’s details or schedules a metadata refresh; full details are still fetched for tracks that actually play.

In Marvin Schenkel’s cold-cache lab run using the same 133 tracks, requests fell from 222 to 127 and the measured time from 88.5 seconds to 12.5 seconds. The shared request allowance also rises from five requests per two seconds to ten per second. Music Assistant still slows down when YouTube returns a rate-limit response; neither measured run received one.

pullRequests.title: Start YouTube Music Endless Mixes in seconds again

articles.title: Music Assistant plays Apple Music purchases that remain licensed
articles.dek: Purchased tracks reappear after a manual sync when Apple still offers them.
body: Music Assistant restores playback for iTunes purchases that Apple still licenses, instead of marking every purchase-only track unavailable. It checks the purchase against Apple’s catalog and uses the playable audio format and purchase identifier for the license request.

In contributor anthonws’s library, thirteen of twenty-four purchases became available; eleven tracks from the U2 giveaway remained unavailable. A manual provider sync is needed to refresh the stored availability. Purchases Apple no longer licenses stay excluded.

pullRequests.title: Play Apple Music purchases that Apple still sells

articles.title: LIFX Moods join Home Assistant lighting controls
articles.dek: A mood can apply across several lights while preserving their brightness.
body: Home Assistant adds LIFX Moods, the color selections that replace Themes in LIFX’s phone app. Multizone and matrix lights get a Mood selector, and a new action can apply one mood across a group of LIFX lights without changing their individual brightness.
Only Moods that LIFX does not restrict by location are included. Existing Theme controls remain, so adopting Moods does not require replacing those automations.

pullRequests.title: Add support for non-geofenced LIFX Moods

articles.title: System Bridge gives Home Assistant its own sign-in key
articles.dek: Access can be revoked for one client without changing the shared credential for everyone.
body: Home Assistant signs in to System Bridge with its own client key instead of the API token shared by every client. System Bridge can then sign out that Home Assistant connection independently.

Setup accepts a key, a pairing code or a pasted pairing link. Existing connections exchange their saved token for a key during setup; an unreachable computer is retried, while a refused token asks the owner to sign in again. Pairing the same Home Assistant instance again replaces its key rather than creating another client.

pullRequests.title: Sign in to System Bridge with a key of its own

articles.title: Home Assistant updates Z-Wave devices without waiting for sleeping ones
articles.dek: Update all queues other devices while the radio still transfers one firmware at a time.
body: Home Assistant’s Update all operation for Z-Wave firmware no longer waits for a sleeping device before requesting updates for the others. It makes use of Z-Wave JS’s update queue, while firmware transfers still run one device at a time.

Controller firmware remains separate from device updates. When requested together, device updates start first and the controller waits for them. A new device update fails if the controller is already updating, because that operation restarts the driver.

pullRequests.title: Allow parallel Z-Wave firmware updates on different nodes

articles.title: Plex sees listening through every Music Assistant player
articles.dek: Chromecasts, browser players and the app regain Now Playing and listening history.
body: Music Assistant reports Plex playback from players that do not have a Plex Connect instance. A Chromecast, browser player or the app can therefore appear in Plex’s Now Playing and listening history, rather than leaving that listening session invisible.

Start, pause, resume, skip and stop are reported promptly, with progress updates every thirty seconds. A synchronized group appears once under its lead player, and an existing Plex Connect player keeps the same device identity.

pullRequests.title: Report Plex playback in Plex for players without Plex Connect

articles.title: Music Assistant prevents account changes from mixing music libraries
articles.dek: Switching a provider’s account requires removing it and adding it again.
body: Music Assistant keeps a music provider tied to the account used during setup. Signing in to a different account while reconfiguring it is refused, with instructions to remove the provider and add it again; signing back into the same account continues to work.

The change prevents old playlists and cached information remaining after an account switch, followed by the next sync replacing that provider’s library content. YouTube Music, Tidal, SoundCloud and Spotify identify their account without an extra service request. A failed reconfiguration restores the previous sign-in.

pullRequests.title: Keep a music provider on the account it was set up with

articles.title: Swiss departure sensors can show trains without bus detours
articles.dek: A transport filter separates direct train choices from journeys that start with a walk.
body: Home Assistant’s Swiss public-transport setup can limit a route to selected transport types: train, tram, ship, bus or cableway. This keeps alternatives such as a walk to a nearby bus stop out of a train-only departure sensor.
The chosen modes become part of the connection’s identity, so filtered and unfiltered versions of the same route can coexist. Existing connections keep their unfiltered results.

pullRequests.title: Add means of transport filter to Swiss public transport

articles.title: NINA keeps every selected warning region
articles.dek: Regions following a duplicate regional code no longer disappear from setup.
body: Home Assistant’s NINA setup preserves all the regions a person selects for warnings. Choosing municipalities that shared a regional code could previously stop processing the selection early, silently dropping later regions.
Municipalities with the same code now share a combined label, and setup continues through the remaining choices. Shivansh Shukla makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction.

pullRequests.title: Fix dropping of selected regions in NINA config flow

articles.title: Home Assistant can connect to OpenWrt over HTTPS
articles.dek: New setup options enable encrypted connections and certificate checks.
body: Home Assistant’s OpenWrt connection adds an HTTPS option, with certificate verification enabled by default when encryption is selected. This gives owners a protected connection to the router’s management interface.
Existing configurations continue to use HTTP unless changed; the update does not silently enable encryption. Rudd-O makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the addition.

pullRequests.title: Add SSL support to the OpenWrt (ubus) integration

articles.title: Z-Wave JS UI refreshes neighbor information across the network
articles.dek: One Mesh-page action replaces checking devices individually, with a warning before the radio is interrupted.
body: Z-Wave JS UI adds a Refresh neighbors button to its Mesh page, updating every device’s neighbor information in one action. The refreshed details appear in graph hover cards and device panels; previously, refreshing required opening devices one at a time.

The button asks for confirmation because the controller turns its radio off while reading the tables, then counts down the sixty-second wait before another refresh. Steve Berg tested the action on a network of about thirty-seven devices. This is his first contribution to Z-Wave JS UI.

pullRequests.title: feat(ui): refresh all neighbors from the mesh page
